To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
dissociated embryonic brain tissue suspensions may be injected into the depth of adult brains, where they survive and grow to innervate the host brain parenchyma.

1) dissociated embryonic brain cell suspensions can be grafted into the adult brain, 2) the grafts survive and grow, 3) they can mediate considerable functional recovery, 4) they can replace lost cells in the host brain, and 5) they can be used to study the mechanisms of axonal outgrowth and synapse formation.
dissociated CNS tissue can be successfully transplanted into deep brain sites and that the grafted cells can mediate considerable functional recovery of previously denervated host tissue.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and use of new methods to facilitate the analysis of the mechanisms of neuronal reconstruction.
the development of methods for transplantation of central nervous tissue into adult brains and with the study of the fate and functional properties of such grafted neurons.
the study of the development of neuronal systems in the central nervous system of mammals and the use of these data for the development of new therapeutic approaches in neurology and psychiatry.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

neuronal transplantation is an experimental tool of the utmost value for the investigation of neuronal replacement, neuronal regeneration, and the reestablishment of synaptic connections after brain damage.
the present study has provided evidence that the transplantation technique used is a useful method for the investigation of neuronal reconstruction following brain damage.

the present study provides a new approach for the intraparenchimal injection of dissociated CNS suspensions, and it demonstrates that such grafted neurons can reinnervate a previously denervate host brain region, and that they can replace neurons in a target region damaged by a neurotoxic agent.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the transplantation of dissociated embryonic brain tissue to the adult rat brain can be accomplished with relative ease and with a high survival of grafted cells.
neuronal transplantation may provide a powerful new tool to study the mechanisms by which neurons and glia interact in normal and abnormal nervous tissue.
the dissociated cell suspensions can be used to replace the neurons in the brain regions which are damaged by neurotoxins.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to transplant dissociated neuronal cells into the adult brain and that they can survive, grow, and integrate into host tissue.
dissociated cell suspensions can be used for transplantation to deep brain targets.
dissociated CNS tissue can be transplanted by direct intraparenchylmal injections.
